requirements.text: 6+ years of hands-on quantitative software engineering, quantitative development, market risk technology, or closely related production engineering experience in complex financial environments.
Strong hands-on development expertise in Python OR Java; deep expertise in both languages is not required.
Experience implementing, enhancing, testing, and supporting production-grade quantitative analytics, financial calculations, market-risk applications, or risk-processing platforms.

Experience in Capital Markets, Market Risk, Risk Technology, quantitative engineering, or a closely related financial-services environment, with practical exposure to financial products or risk analytics.
Strong analytical and numerical problem-solving skills, including experience with financial time-series or market/risk datasets, calculation validation, reconciliation, and troubleshooting.

Ability to collaborate with Quant, Market Risk, Front Office, and Engineering stakeholders and convert quantitative methodologies or loosely defined analytical requirements into reliable production software.
Direct hands-on experience delivering FRTB IMA technology or analytics solutions is highly preferred.
Experience implementing or supporting Risk Factor Eligibility Testing (RFET), FRTB market-risk analytics, or related regulatory risk capabilities.
Experience with enterprise Market Risk platforms, internal risk engines, regulatory capital technology, VaR, sensitivities, or other market-risk analytics.
Knowledge of regulatory capital calculations, risk factor modelling, quantitative risk methodologies, risk model validation, or related Market Risk techniques.
Experience implementing or validating analytics on large-scale financial time-series, risk-factor, or market-data datasets.
Experience with market data sourcing, enrichment, risk factor data management, or Bloomberg data integration.
Knowledge of Rates, Credit, and/or Equity products and associated market-risk analytics.
Experience integrating modern strategic platforms with complex legacy risk infrastructure.
Exposure to both Python and Java environments is beneficial, although deep expertise in one primary stack is sufficient.
